unit.why: A first-person memorate: the narrator, a student in the tsaddik's yeshiva, raises a halakhic objection on Shabbat ha-Gadol, the master checks it and answers, and then explains why Torah debate proceeds through questions and answers.
unit.boundary_note: section 25 in the next division is a separate tale told right after this one ('ואח״כ מיד סיפר')

stories.start_quote: וראינו בחוש כי כל פלפוליו היו
stories.summary_en: Before Pesach the tsaddik was teaching the rule that fruit juice does not cause leavening. On Shabbat ha-Gadol a student, the narrator, cited a law that seemed to contradict him, and the tsaddik stood astonished while the student trembled. The tsaddik studied the law in his room, came back to show there was no contradiction, and explained mystically that questions and answers break the husks and screens, so that a law rooted above can be drawn down into this world.
